title: Coordinate expansion of a continuous linear functional
statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite index set and let $L \colon \bbr^{\iota} \to \bbr$ be a continuous linear functional. Writing $e_i$ for the standard basis vector whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ and whose other coordinates are $0$, every vector $z \in \bbr^{\iota}$ satisfies
\[
  L(z) \;=\; \sum_{i \in \iota} z_i \, L(e_i).
\]
hypotheses_covered: L is a continuous linear functional on ℝ^ι
z is a vector in ℝ^ι
replaced:
Let $\iota$ be a finite type and $L$ a continuous linear functional on $\iota \to \bbr$. Then for every $z : \iota \to \bbr$,
\[
  L(z) \;=\; \sum_{i \in \iota} z_i \, L(e_i),
\]
where $e_i$ is the standard basis vector $\mathrm{Pi.single}\,i\,1$.
